description: A project's claims, each with its label (what a paper's \label and a citation name it by, e.g. 'thm:d5-rank5'), its number, its statement (Markdown with formulas), its status and what it rests on. A project writes them on one of two scales, answered as 'scale' with its 'statuses' and 'kinds': 'math' — theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture, question; 'open' (not proved), 'paper' (proved on paper), 'computer' (by a computation), 'lean' (formalised in Lean), 'refuted', 'retracted' (taken back — the † of a result) — or 'law' — position, conclusion, risk, obligation; 'draft', 'agreed', 'practice' (confirmed by practice), 'disputed', 'outdated' (the norm under it changed). set_claim_scale chooses it. A basis is a wiki page with the proof ('page', its id and title — or 'hidden' where you may not open the page), a computation by the name a [comp:…] cites ('computation'), a Lean declaration ('lean'), a source in words ('source') or a norm of law ('legal': the act on the legal shelf — 'legal.document', its id for get_legal_document, its title and the 'place' cited — with 'changed' true when the act's publisher has said other words since, 'reaches' whether the change is in the place cited (null where that cannot be told), 'changedAt', and 'asOf' — when the text it rests on was received, its edition; a person marks it looked at on the register's screen). This register is where a claim's status is kept: read it here rather than from a page's words, and change it with set_claim_status. Ordered by number, then label. Anybody who sees the project.

kind.description: Only claims of this kind, one of the project's scale.

q.description: Words its label, number, title or statement holds, case aside.

status.description: Only claims of this status, one of the project's scale.
